7253.d:
The "Burning ship" fractal is a surprisingly rich variant of the Mandelbrot. The math differs only a little, but produces amazingly complex imagery.

It is named so, because it looks like a ship on fire with towers in the background.

Zooming into various regions of the fractal, even upto a trillion of magnification, yields unique structures and patterns.

This collection has a carefully curated set of 26 locations within the fractal, which have very diverse shapes and forms.
These are rendered in 6 different palettes with high contrast and saturated colors.
Interestingly there is a slight natural asymmetry in each piece that adds to the character.


Output is 2048x2048 that takes about 10 seconds to render

Best viewed fullscreen.

A hunting party stalks its prey through the dead of night. 

I was inspired by old computer games that I used to play in grade school. You know, floppy drive type stuff. There is a little (or maybe a lot?) of Oregon Trail in this piece. The goal was to make something that feels like an old game but takes advantage of modern technology to create a scene that has a bit of drama. I decided not to define a rarity value to any of the features, and to instead see what comes out as rare naturally. 

Randomized Features

- Moon size and position
- Forest size, or height on the canvas
- Tree size
- Tree sway direction
- Tree sway duration
- Tree sway speed
- Tree sprites
- Tree colors
- % of dead trees
- Position of the Deer
- Position of the Party
- Number of Party members

7270.d:
A monolith is a geological feature consisting of a single massive stone or rock, such as some mountains. Its meaning comes from ancient greek, composed by the words μόνος ("one" or "single") and λίϑος ("stone"). This singularity is represented by the uniqueness of each minting.

The work is done in WebGL using Threejs, with custom shaders for volumetric lighting to give it a more mystical, unique aesthetics.

Variations are:
- Color
- Resolution of the monolith
- Particles Amount
- Rarity

The work has 4 levels of rarity:
- Common
- Uncommon
- Rare
- Ultrarare

Uncommon, Rare and Ultrare are more shiny and are respectively colored: Silver, Gold and Fiery Gold.

Also, rarity determines the number of vertical resolution, resulting in some cases in monoliths that resemble the shape of flowers.

Algorithm is based on a "Zoning Resolution Law" from 1916.

In order to provide access to sunlight on the ground level and on nearby streets, the zoning rules determine maximum buildings' mass - the shape and height of skyscrapers.

Basing on these rules algorithm can generate millions of unique procedural buildings variations using parameters like:
lot size, district class, streets width, city grid, maximum height etc.

Available districts classes: ·1¼, ·1½, ·2, ·2½

The SSS-V2 is a self-contained autonomous system for the creation and management of elementary units, also known as hex-points. It is well known that elementary units are fragile to the environment and constantly break, which is why SSS-V2 implements a real-time monitoring system to identify failure and repair them swiftly via the defrag-g3 algorithm.

DEBUGGING
==========
It has been reported that in some cases SSS-V2 will be unable to successfully repair deeply damaged units. If this happens please do not reboot the system, and wait for SSS-V2 to reinitialize gracefully. 

Please report any further issues at @sketchboi64.

Intertwined began as a study of how to overlap randomized shapes at many intersection points while retaining consistency and physical accuracy. I initially envisioned vines growing on buildings, but over time Intertwined moved in a more abstract embroidery-like direction while retaining influences from that foundational concept.

Controls:
Key S: Save the output as a jpeg at the current resolution (only available once the piece has finished loading).
Key Arrow Up: Scale the resolution up by a multiple of 1080 pixels. There is no maximum. The current highest recommended scale-factor is 4x.
Key Arrow Down: Scale the resolution down by a multiple of 1080 pixels. 1080p is the minimum.
Key A: Skip the construction animation to show the final result immediately (please note that for pieces with a larger grid skipping the animation may cause a long pause).

Browser Support: Confirmed to work in Chrome Version 97.0.4692.71

"Bamboo" aims to capture the adventures I would envision while looking at that small jungle in my garden.

Inspiration was drawn from pointillism, botanical illustration and naive art.

The piece is purely generative, in the sense of painting the picture with code via p5js points and shapes, no assets are used.

Generative parameters include density of elements, parameters of elements and color.

The symbol of the trefoil knot has known from ancient times as triquetra. Triquetra is a work derived from Latin tri- (three) and quetrus (cornered). Its original meaning was simply "triangle" and it has been used to refer to various three-cornered shapes.

In the mathematical field of topology, knot theory is the study of mathematical knots. While inspired by knots which appear in daily life, such as those in shoelaces and rope, a mathematical knot differs in that the ends are joined so it cannot be undone, the simplest knot being a ring.

A fundamental problem in knot theory is determining when two descriptions represent the same knot.
A complete algorithmic solution to this problem exists, which has unknown complexity.

Accretion's aim is to be work which is soothing and interesting to look at whilst it is forming as well as beautiful to look at as a completed piece.

Visuals can be toggled between 'blueprint' mode which outlines the containers and displays the palettes by pressing the 'b' button on the keyboard (or swiping up on mobile).

Double particle mode can be enabled by pressing the 'p' button on the keyboard, which increases rate at which the containers will fill. Be aware that this will come with a performance cost.

Depending on container size, Accretion can take several minutes to finish so be patient.
Due to the way particles are generated and tracked, resizing the browser will restart the animation.

Made with p5js with a modicum of love 💙.

7385.d:
Experimental generative collection that merges analog photography, AI, generative text, and algorithmic coding, by digging down into the essence and building blocks of the different artistic communication channels. 

This work engages with all aforementioned mediums in a joint manner, guided by a random process. It starts with a collection of analog photographs, shot on film and scanned that were later used as a training dataset in Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) training. This way, A.I. learns the main characteristics of film photography. In particular, it mimics its recognizable grain. Another type of pixel grain is added with the use of code and pixel shifting as well as digital manipulation. Finally, the last type of “grain” appears with the use of generative text where a different kind of A.I. was given a short description of the project and instructed to imagine the rest of the story. The fragmented and void of meaning parts of generative text are added to the images as one of the possible traits.

7413.d:
"Now you will see them better, even in the darkness."
—Thomas Ligotti, 'Flowers of the Abyss'

Two modified versions of the Gumowski/Mira strange attractor map produce overlapping chaotic paths. Whilst rendering, an image forms over either a textured background. Each frame draws eight-thousand, one-hundred and ninety-two iterations of the attractors, then slightly-altered seed values are taken and the process begins again.

After a further ninety-five frames, a full seventy hundred and eighty-six thousand, four-hundred and thirty-two points have been rendered to the canvas, and the piece is complete. That's a lot of calculations, so patience is rewarded as the image forms.

At any time during the rendering process, a high-resolution version can be saved by pressing 'S'.

7421.d:
Procedurally generated maps inspired by old portolan charts.

These nautical maps were first created mapping the Mediterranean in the 13th century and were based on rhumb-line networks.

The compass lines are supposed to be lines of constant bearing at sea but were often inaccurate.

This is my attempt at capturing the chaotic look of these old handdrawn charts using mainly simple strokes and lines. 

Everything apart from the ship and the frame is drawn using simple canvas operations.

Features:
5 Color sets
Land Fill: Zigzag or solid 
Water fill 
Colored coasts  
Framed 
Kraken
Maelstrom 
Typhoon 


Further, the island amount and shapes, the look of the mountains, compass, city and map names, type of waves and the rhumb network are randomized in each iteration.

Some features may not appear if there is not enough water available.

Previews may look slightly different.

S to save
Space to pause

Resources:
rough.js
hull.js
opentype.js
https://github.com/ctrlcctrlv/QuaeriteRegnumDei

Inspired on a medieval painting of the Virgin pregnant with the sun. 
Shape has been removed and it has been synthesized into its primarial colours: blue, red and yellow. As soon as the figurative image is taken out, the symbolism comes out clearly. The union of heaven and earth reveals the Phylosopher's Stone. A sunrise where the Above finds the Below (As above so below, Esmerald Table). 

LVI (56) editions. 

Created by @mehno_art.

7440.d:
Generative Gestures. Algorithmic Abstraction. Brushstrokes generated with code, nested & compressed into a shaped canvas. These are the expressionist paintings a computer would dream up.

Four rarity features are listed below. Other traits also contribute to the output but are not part of the rarity calculation, e.g. stroke weight, gestural complexity, and colors, which are chosen randomly (no defined palettes).

Layers: 1-7
Determines the number of gestures that are layered on top of one another. "7 Layers" is the rarest outcome at ~2% expected occurrence; 1 & 6 Layers are the 2nd rarest at ~4%.

Closed Loops: Yes/No
Determines whether the gestures close in on themselves, creating an infinite line (it's not always obvious by looking at the image). ~30% expected chance of Closed Loop output.

Dark Mode: Yes/No
Dim the lights. ~10% expected rate.

Transparency: Yes/No
Brushstrokes overlap each other with a combination of various transparency modes, creating even more unpredictable beauty. ~10% expected rate.

This work shows the gravitational vector field from two such bodies. Occasionally, lines will also show curves of equipotential in this field, the centre of mass of the system, the orbital paths traced out. The system is periodic and will loop forever.

Press UP to export one second of frames, and DOWN to save an SVG from the current frame.

7499.d:
Fanfàrria (Catalan for fanfare), a musical piece often played by trumpets in local town parties.

A mix of detailed handcrafted watercolor strips drawn in a generative motion that create an illusion of a trail of feathers. The different variations are based on the variance of color in the feathers and the motion of the trail.

Less variance on the feathers is rearer.
